label: rem:ns-obstruction-computation-interpretation
title: Topological and analytic terms occupy complementary tower subgroups
html: Scope of the computation. Part (a) identifies the global surface Euler class e(\xi) = -6 \in H^2(\Sigma_4, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} of the Reeb bundle on Bring's surface — the non-zero global obstruction \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) of NS-regular QOU — together with the excision isomorphism H^2_{\{p\}}(\Sigma_4, \mathbb{Z}) \cong H^2(D^2, S^1; \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} by which e(\xi) localises as the Poincaré--Hopf index sum \sum_p \mathrm{ind}_p(s) = -6 of a chosen section s. By contrast, the complementary-subgroup decomposition \kappa_n|_\Sigma = \mathrm{lk}\cdot e(\xi)|_\Sigma + \delta_n|_\Sigma on a one-dimensional collision curve \Sigma (parts (c)--(d)) does not hold: H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0 forces the curve restriction to vanish identically, H^2(\Sigma_4, \mathcal{O}_{\Sigma_4}) = 0 forces the sheaf-cohomological jet corrections \delta_n to vanish, and the Biot--Savart jet rate |j^n v| \sim (T^* - t)^{-(n+1)/2} in part (b) is a pointwise scaling ansatz rather than a cohomology class.
